sc2wm.title: SC²-WM: A Self-Correcting World Model with Closed-Loop Feedback for Vision-and-Language Navigation in Continuous Environments
sc2wm.authors: Xuan Yao; Yuze Zhu; Junyu Gao; Zongmeng Wang; Changsheng Xu
sc2wm.problem: RGB-D VLN-CE under partial observability and scene shift. The agent predicts waypoints, maintains a topological map and selects actions from an instruction plus observation history. Panoramic and monocular configurations have materially different sensory access.
sc2wm.mechanism: Sections 3.1–3.3, pp. 3–6: visual features first retrieve recent episodic features using attention with relative spatial/time cues and temporal decay; a gate blends current and retrieved representations. An observation-conditioned posterior updates latent s_t. A provisional policy proposes an action, and a Transformer prior predicts its next latent mean. Equation 9 defines Δ_t = predicted s_(t+1) − s_t. A learned residual/gating network ψ(s_t,Δ_t) produces a refined current state, from which the final policy selects the executed action. This Δ is an endogenous predicted state change, not an observed next-state prediction error, and the paper explicitly says it is not a target to minimize. Training combines teacher action cross-entropy on original/refined states (Eq. 11), posterior/prior KL (Eq. 12), and decoded future-feature squared error (Eq. 13). Test-time adaptation compares provisional versus final action distributions by KL, uses a running percentile plus a low-entropy condition, and updates world-model parameters through reconstruction loss (Eq. 14); policy parameters are excluded according to the text. Thus there are separate immediate inference refinement and gradient adaptation mechanisms.
sc2wm.novelty: Relative to NavMorph's forward memory updates and HNR's predicted feature tree, SC²-WM adds provisional-action latent refinement and conditional gradient adaptation. These are combinations of recurrent world modeling, episodic visual calibration and test-time optimization; they do not establish statistical calibration or a causal correctness guarantee.
sc2wm.results: PAPER EXPERIMENT: Table 3 p. 8, monocular R2R-CE val-unseen: reproduced base SR 43.77/SPL 29.39; state correction 48.34/33.02; plus visual calibration 49.86/36.05; full 50.90/37.17; fixed-interval adaptation 50.30/36.58; removing reconstruction 48.89/34.58. These ablations support the combined recipe and modest trigger benefit, but do not isolate whether Δ is reliable under confidently wrong dynamics. Table 1 p. 7 HNR panoramic base 61/51 to 66/54, test 58/50 to 62/53. Training is reported on one RTX3090, under 40 hours (p. 8); no runtime independently measured.
sc2wm.bottleneck: The feedback signal can be large for a correct motion and small for an incorrect but stationary latent prediction; low action entropy does not imply correctness. Algorithm 2 p. 6 uses d (predicted s_(t+1)) versus current calibrated v_t, whereas Eq. 13 and prose use next observation v_(t+1). Timing/target discrepancy requires source-level resolution before implementation. Also distinguish dynamic percentile described in text from fixed τ notation in Algorithm 2. These are methodological/reproducibility uncertainties, not demonstrated benchmark failures. The supplement and released code resolve the broad feedback concern: a delayed comparison with actual observations does exist. Remaining uncertainty concerns which parameters/trigger are used, prediction-target alignment and confidence under shift, not the absence of observed residual correction.
sc2wm.followups: NavMorph, HNR, UNeMo; outside-corpus WorldMAP and PiJEPA are relevant current leads, not yet read in this dossier.
associated: SC2-WM (arXiv).pdf: all 18 pages compared at the extracted-token level. Only the first-page arXiv stamp differs from the main PDF; method, tables and supplement text are identical.
sc2wm.access: Both supplied 18-page versions include the same substantive supplement. Appendix pp. 15–16 explicitly defines delayed forecast-to-real-observation alignment (FRL); Table 6 gives SR 49.86 without adaptation, 49.48 for entropy minimization, 50.19 asynchronous and 50.90 FRL. Reported runtime rises from 17.78 to 18.92 seconds. Pages 17–18 report 500 physical robot runs (100 trials for each of five configurations), a 1.5 m success criterion and offboard/asynchronous processing; these are author experiments, not reproduced. The immediate endogenous delta is not the same quantity as this delayed residual. Source discrepancies are recorded in the implementation audit.

navmorph.title: NavMorph: A Self-Evolving World Model for Vision-and-Language Navigation in Continuous Environments
navmorph.authors: Xuan Yao; Junyu Gao; Changsheng Xu
navmorph.problem: Continuous instruction navigation with RGB-D observations, predicted waypoints and accumulated experience. Addresses latent foresight and online scene adaptation without repeatedly synthesizing RGB panoramas.
navmorph.mechanism: Sections 3.1–3.4 pp. 3–6: a recurrent state-space model combines deterministic history h_t with Gaussian stochastic state s_t. Observation-conditioned posterior and action-conditioned prior share the latent dynamics. Contextual Evolution Memory stores N_m scene vectors; top-K cosine retrieval enriches h_t with a weighted memory sum (Eq. 2), and retrieved slots receive exponential forward updates v_k←(1−β) v_k+βh_t (Eq. 3). The prior then rolls out T_p future states/actions without future observations. A decoder reconstructs visual embeddings rather than RGB. Eq. 5 combines observed/future feature likelihoods, action likelihoods and Gaussian posterior/prior KL. Eq. 6 adds NDTW-style temporal alignment, with L2 supervision for continuous displacement, plus DAgger-like teacher-node cross-entropy. At test time memory is updated forward; this 'self-evolution' is not gradient-based TTA. The policy still depends on pretrained navigational architectures ETPNav/HNR or monocular VLN-3DFF.
navmorph.novelty: The navigation-specific contribution is context-memory augmentation of RSSM and online memory evolution, relative to PlaNet/Dreamer recurrent dynamics and HNR feature anticipation. Future-feature losses and memory changes must be separated experimentally; they are not a new general principle of world modeling.
navmorph.results: PAPER EXPERIMENT: Table 1 p. 7 monocular reproduced VLN-3DFF SR 43.8/SPL 29.4 versus NavMorph 47.9/33.2 on R2R-CE val-unseen; test 43.8/28.6 versus 45.7/30.2. HNR panoramic 61/51 to 64/53. Table 2 RxR-CE HNR56.48/46.62 to 58.02/48.98. Section 4.3 describes loss and fixed-memory ablations; numerical Table 3 is not transcribed here. Results establish additive gains on these architectures, not uniformly superior cross-protocol navigation. Reported single RTX3090 training; compute not reproduced. Table 3, p. 8: removing reconstruction/action/KL yields SR 45.51/44.81/44.10 versus 47.91 full; without self-evolution it is 45.08. Table 4 gives 21.22 seconds per instruction for contextual memory versus 44.56 for the LSTM adaptation variant. Memory size 1000 gives the best SR in Figure 4, while both smaller and larger settings can hurt. The authors explicitly acknowledge cross-episode test-scene memory and evaluation-fairness concerns.
navmorph.bottleneck: CEM may retain scene/context biases across episodes and depends on slot replacement, reset policy and episode order. No confidence gate distinguishes helpful versus harmful stored features in Eq. 2–3. Predicted-state alignment is not a calibrated uncertainty estimate. SC²-WM subsequently adds latent refinement and gradient adaptation, partly addressing online correction but retaining uncertainty about endogenous feedback validity. Methodological limitation; confidence medium.
navmorph.followups: SC²-WM Sections 3 and Table 3 directly extend the world-model adaptation theme; HNR remains a necessary controlled baseline.

hnr.title: Lookahead Exploration with Neural Radiance Representation for Continuous Vision-Language Navigation
hnr.authors: Zihan Wang; Xiangyang Li; Jiahao Yang; Yeqi Liu; Junjie Hu; Ming Jiang; Shuqiang Jiang
hnr.problem: A waypoint's current single-view feature misses occluded future context; RGB generation can be slow and distorted. Assumes panoramic 12-view RGB-D, camera pose/intrinsics, predicted candidate waypoints and low-level control.
hnr.mechanism: Section 3 pp. 3–6: frozen CLIP ViT-B/32 grid features are backprojected with depth/pose into an incremental 3D feature cloud (Eq. 1–3). For a candidate camera ray, k-nearest cloud features plus relative position/orientation/scale feed an MLP predicting feature vector and volume density; volumetric compositing gives region embeddings (Eq. 4–8). Empty neighborhoods skip the MLP. A four-layer view Transformer inpaints contextual information in feature space; region/view cosine losses match CLIP targets, with RGB-D rendering auxiliary loss (Eq. 9–12). HNR pretraining uses 800 HM3D training scenes and random 15-step episodes. Candidate 12-view features and predicted depth generate next-level waypoint/lookahead nodes. A panorama encoder and graph-aware cross-modal Transformer score visited, candidate, lookahead and stop nodes. Branch scores are max (candidate, descendant scores), Eq. 15. Soft-target cross-entropy supervises the branch leading closest to the goal; Dijkstra plus a controller executes the chosen reachable waypoint. This is explicit inference-time feature lookahead, not merely a training loss.
hnr.novelty: Compared with DREAMWALKER's RGB scene synthesis/MCTS and RNR-Map's 2 D latent map, HNR uses a 3D feature cloud, multiscale semantic rendering, and parallel branch scoring. It inherits graph-aware navigation machinery from ETPNav/DUET lineage. Extra HM3D pretraining must be accounted for when attributing all gains to geometry.
hnr.results: PAPER EXPERIMENT: Table 3 p. 7 holds lookahead policy constant: single-view SR 57.21/SPL 49.15; NeRF RGB56.55/48.61; image generation 58.35/50.96; HNR60.74/51.27; oracle future features 63.13/54.59. This is stronger mechanism evidence than leaderboard comparison. Removing positional embeddings gives 56.17/48.91; removing region loss 60.20/50.74. Fig. 5 p. 7 reports feature similarity decreasing with prediction distance. Table 1 R2R-CE unseen SR 61/SPL 51 versus ETPNav 57/49; Table 2 RxR-CE56.39/46.73 versus 54.79/44.89. Table 5, p. 8 reports rendering at 11.5 ms on one RTX 3090, versus 169.5 ms without sparse sampling and 42.3 ms without KD-tree search. This is component timing. Table 6 gives SR 60.74 for soft supervision versus 56.72 for the hard-target variant; the authors attribute the latter to occlusion and prediction noise.
hnr.bottleneck: Blind-region semantic extrapolation deteriorates with distance, and max over noisy descendant scores can favor an overoptimistic branch. No uncertainty penalty or calibration is included in Eq. 15. Large geometric feature memory and 800-scene pretraining are costs. NavMorph and SC²-WM add adaptation; NavQ replaces rollouts with semantic successor features in a different discrete/object-goal protocol. No evidence here that those eliminate HNR's unseen-occlusion error under equal sensing/data.
hnr.followups: NavMorph; SC²-WM; NavQ. DREAMWALKER's oracle-world and oracle-distance analyses motivate separating prediction from scoring errors.

dreamwalker.title: DREAMWALKER: Mental Planning for Continuous Vision-Language Navigation
dreamwalker.authors: Hanqing Wang; Wei Liang; Luc Van Gool; Wenguan Wang
dreamwalker.problem: Long-horizon decision making in freely traversable continuous environments; assumes 360°RGB-D, a pretrained waypoint predictor and low-level 15°turn/0.25 m forward actions. Success means stopping within 3 m, at most 500 steps.
dreamwalker.mechanism: Sections 3.1–3.2 pp. 3–6: episodic environment graph stores visited panorama features and geometric edges; a scene synthesizer projects observed RGB-D into a candidate camera frame and inpaints a plausible panorama via a Pathdreamer-style two-stage generator. Imagined observations recursively extend possible paths. MCTS selects using UCT Q+C√(logN/N_a), expands a node, rolls out to horizon K, and backs up discounted reward. A language-conditioned graph-attention network estimates distance-to-go for each graph node; this supplies search rewards and rollout preference. Execute the best root action, observe reality, update the graph, and replan. Distance model training uses true and randomly synthesized nodes with L2 shortest-distance supervision; scene generator/waypoint model are separately trained. Default 50 search iterations, horizon 4, discount 0.98. The policy is not trained end-to-end through a differentiable search.
dreamwalker.novelty: The paper integrates an explicit episodic graph and scene generator as a discrete mental testbed for MCTS in VLN-CE; Pathdreamer supplied visual forecasting and Look Before You Leap supplied earlier imagined-planning ideas. The contribution is their structured continuous-navigation integration, not first world-model navigation.
dreamwalker.results: PAPER EXPERIMENT: Table 2 p. 7 val-unseen SR 49/SPL 44; oracle imagined views 54/49; nearest-memory copied views 27/24; greedy distance selection 42/36. Fig. 4 replacing distance predictions with ground truth reaches 100%SR at full replacement, revealing evaluator quality as a major bottleneck rather than only imagery fidelity. Table 1 test SR 49/SPL 44. Search compute increases with iterations, with diminishing gains beyond 50; p. 7 reports typical response within 1.5 s, not independently reproduced.
dreamwalker.bottleneck: Learned distance/value errors can dominate scene errors; oracle world improves 5 SR whereas oracle distance is much stronger but privileged. Eq. 11 prints D (s′)−D (s) while saying progress toward goal is rewarded, and Eq. 12 softmaxes positive distances; these apparent sign inconsistencies require released implementation or author clarification. The official URL currently exposes only documentation in retrieved snapshot, so behavior cannot be established from equations alone. HNR directly improves representation and branch evaluation, but does not guarantee reliable goal scoring.
dreamwalker.followups: HNR Table 3; NavQ's future-distance supervision; SC²-WM. Strong current gap is calibrated decision relevance of predictions, not an absence of imagination.

navq.title: NavQ: Learning a Q-Model for Foresighted Vision-and-Language Navigation
navq.authors: Peiran Xu; Xicheng Gong; Yadong Mu
navq.problem: Discrete goal-oriented VLN on REVERIE/SOON. Natural language specifies an object goal, so conventional reward-labelled Q-learning needs scarce instructions. Seeks task-agnostic future semantics from unlabeled scene graphs.
navq.mechanism: Section 3 pp. 3–6: uses DUET global/local graph encoders plus a future branch. Q (T,a) is a vector of discounted future caption features, not scalar expected reward: R (A)+γEπQ (T∪{A},a′), Eq. 6. Targets sum node-caption embeddings weighted by future visitation probability and γ^t, Eq. 8. Rollouts disallow revisits and are constrained to shortest continuations to make actions discriminative. A4-layer Transformer processes interleaved historical node/action tokens and candidate directions; masked-autoencoder warmup precedes MSE target regression. The Q-model is frozen for subsequent agent training. A4-layer graph future encoder cross-attends to instruction features; its output augments DUET fusion. Separate heads predict traversed distance from global features and remaining distance from future features. DUET auxiliary pretraining plus these distance tasks precedes online DAgger finetuning. Optional 1351 HM3D/Gibson scenes train Q without speaker instructions. Stage batch/LR/iterations:128/1 e−5/30 k,32/5 e−5/100k,4/1 e−5/20 k; single 3090 reported.
navq.novelty: Successor-feature-like prediction of text embeddings and a goal-conditioned future graph branch avoid RGB or recurrent test-time rollouts. A*-inspired auxiliary heads are not an admissible A* heuristic or optimality proof. Closest provided competitors are DUET, HNR, VLN-SIG and semantic prior methods.
navq.results: PAPER EXPERIMENT: Table 3 p. 7 matched reproduced baseline SR 48.14/SPL 33.38/RGSPL 21.05; FE only 48.20/33.92/23.14; Q only 48.48/32.22/21.86; full 53.22/38.89/27.12; oracle Q+FE59.27/47.04/31.62. Main-table original DUET differs in visual backbone, acknowledged p. 7; use reproduced baseline for attribution. REVERIE test SR 53.29 vs reportedDUET52.51; substantial val gains shrink on test. SOON test SR 38.59 vs 33.44 but GOAT40.50, so not universally best. Table 4, p. 8: gamma 0/0.3/0.5/0.7 gives SR 51.12/51.95/53.22/50.89. Longer successor aggregation is useful only up to a point in this experiment. The source constructs targets on one stored shortest-path tree, not all equal shortest paths.
navq.bottleneck: Averaging future semantics can erase rare goal evidence; targets are policy/distribution dependent, not probabilities of correct navigation. The p. 5 uniqueness claim for shortest continuation requires tie-breaking/unique shortest paths: a diamond graph permits two equal first actions to one node. Shortest-route assumptions also do not transfer directly to route-faithful R2R or continuous collision constraints. Feature-oracle gap remains substantial. Extra-scene benefit does not establish architecture-only gain.
navq.followups: UNeMo jointly predicts task-conditioned future features; SC²-WM adds online adaptation in CE. Neither is a directly matched resolution of NavQ's aggregated-semantic ambiguity.

unemo.title: UNeMo: Collaborative Visual-Language Reasoning and Navigation via a Multimodal World Model
unemo.authors: Changxin Huang; Lv Tang; Zhaohuan Zhan; Lisha Yu; Runhao Zeng; Zun Liu; Zhengjie Wang; Jianqiang Li
unemo.problem: Discrete R2R and REVERIE with topological maps. Extends NavGPT-2 frozen LLM features or DUET specialist representations so reasoning can anticipate a candidate's full view and influence navigation.
unemo.mechanism: Method pp. 3–4: score graph nodes, select provisional best candidate j, cross-attend its 1×768 partial visual embedding to N×768 instruction features through 3 layers. Two MLPs produce Gaussian mean/variance; reparameterized latent z is concatenated with candidate graph embedding and decoded into predicted full visual state. A second graph-to-prediction cross-attention/residual stack enriches node embeddings before final action scoring. Training retains baseline pretraining and adds modules in finetuning; baseline objective is λbehavior-cloning+DAgger cross-entropy (Eq. 3). The text calls the module a CVAE but does not specify a complete reconstruction/KL objective, latent width, optimizer or all schedule details; these cannot be invented. Eq. 6 with a single key/value predicts a shared attention update to all queries unless multiple tokens or other interactions exist; residual node differences remain. The claimed bidirectionality is joint learning/action-conditioned prediction, not observed error feedback at deployment.
unemo.novelty: Relative to NavGPT-2 linguistic features and VLN-SIG auxiliary semantics, introduces provisional-action-conditioned visual-state prediction plus second-stage decision integration. Related one-step refinement already overlaps world-model planning; evidence does not establish causal reasoning or calibrated dynamics.
unemo.results: PAPER EXPERIMENT: Table 1 p. 6 FlanT5-1.5 B R2R unseen SR 72.1/SPL 61.1 versus NavGPT270/59; test 72.5/61.3 versus 71/60. Table 3–4 p. 7 final-action-only variant 72.9/61.7, joint two-action learning 72.1/60.3, auxiliaryMWM71.5/61.0. The table 1 headline 72.1 differs from the best ablation 72.9 and should not be silently interchanged. REVERIE testSR53.21 vs reproduced 52.61; SPL 35.17 vs reproduced 34.82 but originalDUET36.06. FrozenLLM means no LLM finetuning, not navigation-training-free. Reported 12 GB versus 27 GB compares different backbone sizes and cannot isolate MWM efficiency.
unemo.bottleneck: No complete public training specification/repository has been verified. One predicted state conditions all action candidates and may amplify a wrong provisional choice. Missing CVAE objective and single-key attention detail prevent a faithful implementation audit. Physical-robot validation is future work. The best ablation versus headline configuration mismatch is unresolved; numerical claims remain author-reported.
unemo.followups: SC²-WM offers explicit latent-difference refinement and conditional adaptation, but in differentCE protocol; novelty of any proposed feedback module must distinguish actual residuals from their internal prediction guidance.

sali.title: Planning from Imagination: Episodic Simulation and Episodic Memory for Vision-and-Language Navigation
sali.authors: Yiyuan Pan; Yunzhe Xu; Zhe Liu; Hesheng Wang
sali.problem: Discrete R2R/REVERIE with RGB-D, semantic segmentation and position. Addresses transient imagined views by retaining them in persistent hybrid memory.
sali.mechanism: Sections 3.1–3.3, pp. 3–5: graph memory distinguishes visited/current, reachable-candidate and imagined locations. Features, positions and temporal markers feed separate real/imagined node encoders and instruction-conditioned graph attention. Imagined scores are gated and added to the nearest reachable candidates (Eqs. 3–4). A recurrent imagination tree projects historical depth/semantics into future poses, completes missing structure, adjusts semantics using a room/object dictionary, synthesizes RGB with SPADE and predicts additional waypoints. The tree is merged into persistent memory; cosine similarity minus positional MSE controls capping/pruning (Eq. 1). Separate pretraining uses semantic cross-entropy, depth L1, room-type cross-entropy, GAN/perceptual/feature-matching losses and waypoint heatmap MSE. Navigation pretraining uses masked language, region, action and object-grounding tasks before encoder fine-tuning. The authors report 100,000 pretraining iterations at batch 32 and 20,000 fine-tuning iterations at batch four, using one then four Quadro RTX 8000 GPUs. Inference repeatedly updates the hybrid graph and selects a reachable or stop action.
sali.novelty: Combines Pathdreamer-style generative components with persistent imagined nodes and adaptive graph action fusion, distinguishing it from transient DREAMWALKER branches and HNR feature-only anticipation. It is already strong prior art against proposing simply storing imagination in memory.
sali.results: PAPER EXPERIMENT: Table 1 p. 6 reports R2R unseen SR 82/SPL 78 and test 79/74; ScaleVLN79/70 and 77/68. REVERIE unseen SR 58/RGS 38/RGSPL 28, test 56/34/25. These are author claims, not reproduced. Table 1 also attributes an implausibly strong REVERIE Seq 2 Seq row relative to other named methods; treat cross-paper baseline labels with caution. Fig. 5 stratifies complex room/object instructions. Generated-image quality is visual/PSNR evidence, not proof of correct hidden room layouts. No verified implementation currently permits independent reproduction. Table 2 on p. 7 reports full-system ablation SPL of 70/71 (SR 80/82), whereas the main R2R headline gives SPL 78. These configurations cannot be silently treated as the same experiment; the source does not permit a complete reconciliation.
sali.bottleneck: Persistent imagined nodes risk treating hallucinated evidence as measured truth; score fusion and pruning use heuristics without calibrated source confidence. Room-object dictionary can reinforce atypical-layout errors. Multiple generation modules and sensors add training/data/compute cost; large reported gains need matched-code replication and uncertainty estimates. Later latent/predictive methods shift the pixel-generation cost, but do not settle provenance-aware imagined-memory reliability.
sali.followups: HNR; NavMorph; SC²-WM; GenEx. Each changes prediction/memory representation, not a demonstrated solution to false persistent memory.

eoe.title: Envisioning Outlier Exposure by Large Language Models for Out-of-Distribution Detection
eoe.authors: Chentao Cao; Zhun Zhong; Zhanke Zhou; Yang Liu; Tongliang Liu; Bo Han
eoe.problem: Zero-shot image out-of-distribution detection from known class names and pretrained CLIP. The supplied EOE paper is not a navigation or world-model method; the acronym must not be conflated with a navigation approach.
eoe.mechanism: Section 3 and Algorithm 1, pp. 3–4: prompt an LLM for outlier class names that are visually related but distinct from known classes. Far, near and fine-grained settings use different prompts. Remove lexical overlap, embed known and envisioned labels with CLIP, and compare them to the normalized image embedding. Equation 3 subtracts beta times the largest envisioned-outlier softmax probability from the largest known-class probability; the softmax denominator includes both sets and beta is 0.25. Threshold the resulting scalar for ID/OOD classification. Evaluation reports false positives at a threshold chosen to retain 95% of ID examples. There is no task-specific model training, dynamics model, action policy or future rollout. CLIP pretraining and offline LLM generation remain external dependencies.
eoe.novelty: Compared with MCM's closed set of known labels, ZOC's learned caption generator and CLIPN's extra encoder training, EOE uses prompted negative-label augmentation and an explicit outlier penalty. Semantic novelty detection does not establish calibrated navigation-action risk.
eoe.results: Table 1, p. 5 averages four ID datasets and four OOD datasets: FPR95 0.21/AUROC 99.92 versus MCM 2.68/99.40. CLIPN uses extra data and scores 0.67/99.80. Later results are substantially harder: the ImageNet far-OOD result on pp. 6–8 has FPR95 30.09/AUROC 92.96; near-OOD average is 9.07/98.59; the fine-grained average is 60.52/81.82 versus CLIPN 56.05/83.18. Thus near-perfect small-dataset numbers must not be generalized to all settings. These are paper experiments, not executed reproduction.
eoe.bottleneck: Generated negative labels cannot enumerate all unknown appearances. The ImageNet20 near-OOD setting filters semantic cosine overlap at 0.85, but this does not guarantee coverage of unseen categories or semantic disjointness elsewhere. LLM versions and prompts alter candidate lists. An unsafe or instruction-inconsistent navigation action may involve familiar objects, so transferring this score into action-risk estimation requires navigation-specific labels and tests.
eoe.followups: Use EOE only as adjacent semantic novelty-detection prior art. Its confidence-like score should be compared with, rather than equated to, transition uncertainty and navigation risk.
